Character sprite sheet for a tiny handmade game on a fantasy console with a 128 by 128 pixel screen, authentic hand-pixelled sprite art. The reference image shows only the costume and the proportions of the character; drawing style, resolution and palette follow this description. Each frame is TINY: exactly 16 art pixels wide and 16 art pixels tall, enlarged without smoothing so every art pixel is a crisp, clearly visible square block of the same size on one regular grid; no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients, no texture, no shading noise. Charm through extreme reduction: every pixel counts, chunky cute proportions.

Fixed palette, use only these colours: black #000000, dark navy blue #1D2B53, dark green #008751, rust brown #AB5236, dark grey #5F574F, light grey #C2C3C7, warm white #FFF1E8, red #FF004D, orange #FFA300, peach #FFCCAA. One-pixel outline in black or dark navy around the figure. Very big head with the cap, almost half of the height, so the striped face reads at this tiny size: a broad warm-white stripe over the forehead to the nose, a black stripe through the eye, a warm-white cheek, a black nose tip at the end of a short pointed snout. Dark green cap, red scarf, dark green vest, rust-brown satchel, peach parcel under the arm, short stubby dark grey legs. Side view facing right.

Layout: one row of 5 frames, evenly spaced with wide empty space between them, all at exactly the same scale, feet on one baseline: 1 standing still; 2 walking, front leg forward and back leg back (contact pose); 3 walking, legs together under the body (passing pose, body one pixel higher); 4 walking, the other leg forward (contact pose); 5 walking, legs together (passing pose, body one pixel higher).

The badger courier: an original mascot character, a stout, short-legged badger with a broad black-and-white striped face, wearing a dark green peaked cap with a brass button, a dark green vest with pockets over a cream shirt with rolled-up sleeves, a long red knitted scarf, a brown leather satchel on a shoulder strap, and a brown paper parcel tied with string under one arm.

Isolated on a fully transparent background, no ground, no shadows, no glow, no frame borders, no grid lines. No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.

Location screen of a tiny handmade game for a fantasy console, authentic low-resolution pixel art exactly as that console can show it. The whole screen is only 128 by 128 pixels: the picture is built from crisp square art pixels of one size on one regular grid, 128 art pixels across the whole image width and 128 down its height, each art pixel a clearly visible square block of 8 by 8 image pixels, as if the tiny screen were enlarged without smoothing; no anti-aliasing, no blur, no mixed pixel sizes, no soft gradients, no texture noise.

Fixed palette of exactly 16 colours, use no other colour: black #000000, dark navy blue #1D2B53, dark plum #7E2553, dark green #008751, rust brown #AB5236, dark grey #5F574F, light grey #C2C3C7, warm white #FFF1E8, red #FF004D, orange #FFA300, yellow #FFEC27, bright green #00E436, sky blue #29ADFF, lavender #83769C, pink #FF77A8, peach #FFCCAA. Large flat areas of one colour, one darker colour of the palette as shading, dark navy or black outlines only where shapes need them. Charm through extreme reduction: every object is only a few art pixels big and drawn with as few pixels as possible, simple friendly shapes with clear silhouettes, like a tiny game where every pixel was placed by hand. The ground is assembled from repeating 8 by 8 pixel tiles: the quay stones, the wooden planks and the roof tiles repeat in regular patterns. The sky is a few flat horizontal bands (dark navy at the top with a few single-pixel stars, dark plum, pink, orange at the horizon) with one row of checkerboard dithering between two bands; one or two low flat clouds. The sea is dark navy with short horizontal sky-blue and lavender dashes in regular rows and a few orange dashes below the horizon. The cottage window and the lantern glass are flat yellow; the lighthouse lamp only as a small yellow spot without any beam or rays, no smoke from the chimney, no glow halos (light and smoke are animated separately in the game).

Side view with a fixed camera at standing eye level, no perspective. Composition (square image): the horizon lies at about 36% of the image height. The flat walkable top surface of the quay (stone slabs) is a horizontal band across the whole width from about 58% to 72% of the image height; characters will walk on it. Below 72% the image shows only the plain front wall of the quay in dark stone with no objects (it will be covered by a text box). The harbour-master's cottage stands on the left at the back edge of the quay, about a quarter of the image width, its door at quay level. The lighthouse stands on its rocky headland on the right, its top at about 8% of the image height, about 8 art pixels wide. The short wooden jetty leads from the quay into the water in the middle, the two small boats are moored beside it, seen exactly from the side. Two barrels, a stack of crates, the rope coil and the lantern on its wooden post stand along the back edge of the quay; the middle of the quay surface stays free. Not a photograph, not a 3D render, not a painting, not detailed modern pixel art, no lens flare, no bloom, no light rays.

Location: the small harbour of Lornholm, a fictional island in a northern sea, at dusk. A stone quay with a short wooden jetty runs along the lower third of the picture. Two small wooden fishing boats are moored at the jetty. On a rocky headland on the right stands a white lighthouse with one red band, its lamp lit. On the left a small stone harbour-master's cottage with a lit window and a smoking chimney. On the quay: two barrels, a stack of crates, a coil of rope and an iron lantern on a wooden post. Calm sea, low clouds, a band of orange light at the horizon, the first stars.

Leave the quay in the foreground free of characters: it is a game background, characters are added later as separate sprites.
